nodes.raw_latex:
Suppose that $3\leq m\leq n\leq p$.
Then $p\geq\lceil\frac{mnp}{m+n+p-2}\rceil$ if and only if $p\geq(m-1)(n-1)+1$.
Catalisano, Geramita, and Gimigliano \cite{cgg02} (see also \cite{cgg08})
proved that if $(m-1)(n-1)+1\leq p\leq mn$, then ${\mathrm{grank}}(p,n,m)=p$.
Thus, $\min{\mathrm{trank}}(p,n,m)=p$ in these cases.
ten Berge \cite{tb00} called a $p\times n\times m$-tensor with $(m-1)n<p<mn$ a tall
array or a tall tensor and proved that ${\mathrm{trank}}(p,n,m)=\{p\}$ for these cases
(see \cite[Chapter 6]{ssm16} for another proof).
Here we define a $p\times n\times m$-tensor a semi-tall tensor if
$(m-1)(n-1)+1\leq p\leq (m-1)n$.
We \cite{ssm13,sms15,sms17} studied the plurality of typical ranks 
of semi-tall tensors and proved
that if $(m-1)(n-1)+2\leq p\leq (m-1)n$, then ${\mathrm{trank}}(p,n,m)=\{p,p+1\}$ if there
exists a nonsingular\  bilinear map $\mathbb{R}^m\times \mathbb{R}^n\to \mathbb{R}^{mn-p}$ and
${\mathrm{trank}}(p,n,m)=\{p\}$ otherwise, where a bilinear map
$\varphi\colon V_1\times V_2\to W$ is nonsingular\  if $\varphi(x,y)=0$ 
implies $x=0$ or $y=0$.
